title: The Day the Rowboat Got a Name
skyStory: The moon has grown to sixty-three percent in Aquarius and is busy redesigning boats. It insists the oars should be shaped like question marks. Saturn has drawn up proper blueprints anyway. Mars wants a figurehead shaped like a tiger. Out on the grey bay, a cold fog sits on the water like it is waiting for a ferry that left an hour ago.

reading: The [[Six of Swords]] floats into your morning on a calm patch of water. You know this card. It has been in Nancy's corner all year, the crossing not yet finished, the little boat, and you with an oar. Today the boat needs a name.

Think about it while you do ordinary things: folding laundry, waiting at a light, stirring something on the stove. A good boat name is funny and a little brave. It should make you both laugh and feel like heading out anyway. Text it to Nancy by 7 pm. Rowing is easier when the boat has a name painted on its side, and the Tiger is surprisingly good with a paintbrush.
joel.mission: Come up with a name for the rowboat from the Six of Swords and send it to Nancy with a tiny drawing.
joel.omen: A gull standing on a buoy, perfectly still. The crossing is steadier than it looks from inside.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's stone, for rowing her way
joel.elementWhy: warmth in the bow of the boat

reading: Fog on the shore this morning, thick enough to hide the far side entirely. That is fine. You do not need to see the other shore to know it is there. You have been rowing toward it with real skill, one patient stroke after another.

Somebody will tell you about their own crossing today, a change or a fresh start, and you will know exactly the right thing to say because you have been on the water too. Say it with your whole heart and both hands. Then let Joel's boat name arrive tonight and make you laugh. [[The Star]] glimmers somewhere behind the fog, and it smells like hope.
nancy.mission: Paint, draw or write the rowboat's name somewhere small, on a sticky note, a mug or the edge of a page.
nancy.omen: A foghorn or a long low sound at dusk. The far shore is close enough to hear.

together.text: Agree on one name for the boat you have been rowing all year. Joel proposes, Nancy approves or improves. Once it is named, the crossing counts as officially charted, and the sky promises calm water for the last two days.
